title: Profile the Hot Path, Don't Guess It
objective: Record a suspected bottleneck before opening a profiler, then name the hottest CPU and allocation frames from committed profile files and relate their cost to algorithmic complexity.
whyThisMatters: Experienced engineers still guess wrong about where time goes. A profile is the cheapest way to find that out before you rewrite the wrong function. This task forbids the fix: diagnosis only, with the wrong guess preserved in git.
evidence: A pre-profile hypothesis file naming the suspected hot function, committed before any profile artifact
A CPU profile file (pprof, async-profiler, py-spy, or language equivalent) committed as a file, not a screenshot alone
An allocation or heap profile file for the same workload
A diagnosis note that copies the hottest frame name from the profile and states its sample or time share as a number
A complexity note relating that frame's work to a growth class from MIT 6.006 (e.g. linear scan vs log n lookup) with the measured cost beside it
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The hypothesis file is committed before the first profile file and names a specific function or module.
CPU and allocation/heap profile files are both present in the repository (binary or text export), not screenshots only.
The diagnosis note copies the hottest CPU frame's symbol as it appears in the profile and states its share as a percentage or time from that file.
The complexity note names a growth class for the hot work and places the measured share next to it — no optimization is shipped in this task.
